sources.note: National Humanities Center's own Residential Fellowships page (awarding body's site, nationalhumanitiescenter.org): competition overview, application cycle dates, eligibility checklists, international applicant and stipend information.
National Humanities Center's own FAQ page for the residential fellowship: eligibility requirements, stipend/salary-replacement details, international scholar (J-1) information.

awarding_body.detail: The page is the National Humanities Center's own site and describes the Residential Fellowship as its programme; no aggregator or third party is involved.
awarding_body.quote: The National Humanities Center is a private, nonprofit organization, and the only independent institute dedicated exclusively to advanced study in all areas of the humanities.

deadline.detail: The page publishes the next cycle: applications open July 1, 2027 with a deadline of October 1, 2027 and letters of recommendation due October 8, 2027. This matches the record's deadline_label ('Applications open July 1; deadline October 1; letters of recommendation due October 8') and deadline_date 2027-10-01 exactly. No past deadline is shown.
deadline.quote: The Center will begin accepting applications for the 2028–29 academic year on July 1, 2027 with a deadline of October 1, 2027. ... All materials are due October 1, 2027, except for letters of recommendation, which are due October 8. ... All letters are due by October 8, 2027.

eligibility.detail: All distinct claims confirmed: PhD or equivalent terminal degree held at least five years before applying (with two named fellowship exceptions, Geiss-Hsu and Philip L. Quinn); humanities research that will result in publication; a substantial record of peer-reviewed scholarship beyond the dissertation; applicants from research universities, liberal arts and teaching colleges, HBCUs, HSIs, tribal colleges and universities, international institutions and independent scholars; no citizenship requirement; the Center sponsors J-1 Research Scholar visas.
eligibility.quote: The NHC welcomes applications from faculty at research universities, liberal arts and teaching colleges, Historically Black Colleges Universities, Hispanic-Serving Institutions, tribal colleges and universities, and international institutions, as well as independent scholars. Successful candidates earned a PhD or an equivalent terminal degree in their discipline, such as the MFA, at least five years prior to applying for the fellowship. ... All candidates must be engaged in humanities research that will result in publication. ... Please note that we have no citizenship requirements. International applicants are warmly invited to apply. ... The Center sponsors J-1 (Research Scholar) visa applications for its Fellows who are not U.S. citizens, and can also provide J-2 visas for spouses and children.

funding.detail: The award is a partial salary-replacement stipend, not fully funded: the Center seeks to provide half salary with the home institution expected to cover the remainder, and it adds round-trip travel for the Fellow and accompanying family but no research travel, moving or living expenses.
funding.quote: The stipend amounts awarded are individually determined, according to the needs of the Fellow and the Center's ability to meet them. The Center seeks to provide half salary with the expectation that the Fellow's home institution covers the remaining salary.

degree_levels.detail: The fellowship requires a PhD or relevant terminal degree (e.g., MFA for research-based non-fiction writers); post-docs and doctoral candidates are explicitly not funded. The record's degree_levels claim is confirmed, with the caveat that the five-year-since-degree rule has two named exceptions (Geiss-Hsu Fellowship, Philip L. Quinn Fellowship).
degree_levels.quote: The applicant holds a PhD or relevant terminal degree for their primary discipline (e.g., MFA for research-based non-fiction writers). ... The NHC does not fund post-docs; the applicant must be working on a significant project beyond their dissertation ... The NHC does not fund doctoral research or writing projects. Applicants must have a doctorate or equivalent terminal credentials prior to applying.

recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Annual competition, fixed calendar: applications open July 1, close October 1, letters due October 8. The page rolls to the next cycle around July each year; re-check in July 2027, when the 2029–30 cycle dates replace the 2028–29 dates currently published. As of the 2026-10-12 check the published deadline is for the 2028–29 fellowship year (the 2027–28 competition closed October 1, 2026, so no application window is literally open on the check date). The five-year-since-terminal-degree rule has two exceptions: the Geiss-Hsu Fellowship (Ming-era China) and the Philip L. Quinn Fellowship (early-career female philosopher).

notes_for_reviewer: Every catalogue claim matches the awarding body's own pages as read on 2026-10-12, and the recorded deadline (2027-10-01) is the exact deadline the Center currently publishes for its upcoming 2028–29 cycle, so I judged the record active. One timing point a human may want to note: on 12 October 2026 no application window is literally open — the 2027–28 competition closed on October 1, 2026, and the next window opens July 1, 2027 — but the page presents October 1, 2027 as the current published deadline, so the record is forward-accurate rather than stale. The eligibility wording 'at least five years before applying' is not absolute: the page names the Geiss-Hsu and Philip L. Quinn fellowships as exceptions to the five-year rule.
